key_quote: Please note that you will need to return the form with a voided check, which is required to sign up for ACH.
reading: Bank ownership is evidenced by a voided check, not by micro-deposit or bank-letter verification [F]. A voided check can be forged; the form adds other verifiers (PR02-PR04) [I]
notes: Identical text at https://www.fidelitycharitable.org/docs/EFT-Registration-form.pdf

key_quote: Please provide supporting information to verify your request. The supporting information must be from within the last 3 years.
reading: Applies to updates as well as enrolments: the requester must quote two Fidelity Charitable grant IDs, two check numbers or a reference number. A first-time grantee faces unspecified 'additional verification' [F]. Grant IDs appear on grant letters, so an attacker holding stolen mail or a compromised inbox could know them [I]
notes: Only first-party published knowledge-based check found for any sponsor

key_quote: The email address for the primary contact must only be accessible by one individual. A group shared inbox will not be accepted.
reading: Two primary contacts with different phones and emails are required; the encrypted Grant Details Report goes to them [F]. The form does not say Fidelity calls either contact before changing bank details [F]
notes: Contacts can be replaced on the same form (PR05)

key_quote: E-Signature is not acceptable. Wet signature is required.
reading: Return by mail, overnight or fax. The legal address 'Cannot be a PO box, mail drop, or c/o due to Customer Identification Program bank standards' [F]. Wet signature resists email-only BEC but not forged paper [I]
notes: Fax return channel noted on form

key_quote: This form is used for both new enrollments and updates to banking, contact, or address information.
reading: ACH changes: register, receive an emailed link to a secure form, select 'Update ACH Information', attach supporting documentation [F]. Stripe changes: made in the Stripe dashboard under Stripe's own controls, which Fidelity does not describe [F]. No callback to a known contact is stated on either path [F]
notes: FAQ also says 'ACH enrollment queue may take several weeks'

key_quote: Fidelity Charitable does not currently send an email notifying nonprofits of grants distributed through Stripe.
reading: Conflicts with the nonprofit FAQ: 'grant notices are emailed each Monday to notify you of grants from the week prior' for Stripe enrollees [F]. Which is current cannot be told from public pages [I]
notes: Notices matter because a redirected payout is detected only when the charity notices a missing grant

key_quote: Avoid acting on unexpected payment detail changes communicated through a single channel.
reading: Names 'business email compromise' and messages 'requesting updated payment details or directing funds to a new account' [F]. Addressed to donors, not to grantees or to Fidelity's own bank-change process [F]
notes: Only sponsor page found that names BEC

key_quote: be cautious about using third-party payment processors or tools that require you to provide your account credentials.
reading: Tells donors to access the Giving Account only via Fidelity Charitable's site or 'an approved mobile application' [F]. Bears on credential-passing DAFpay sessions and agent wrappers (batch 36B) [I]
notes: Does not name any processor

key_quote: While we do not currently require EFT enrollment for nonprofit organizations, we encourage you to enroll for more secure grantmaking.
reading: Non-enrolled charities get checks mailed to the address on their Form 990 [F]. EFT page claims 'With 1 in 5 organizations reporting mail fraud, EFT helps protect grants' (source of the statistic not given) [F]
notes: Check rail redirect vector is mail theft/washing rather than BEC

key_quote: Vanguard Charitable is now issuing Grant Payments with PayPal.
reading: Charities sign up at paypal.com/charities or use a PayPal account 'that has confirmed charity status' [F]. Bank details sit with PayPal, so a bank-change request to Vanguard has no field to change [I]. Page links a video 'How to properly secure your Grant Payments account' (YouTube; not viewed)
notes: Information Vanguard may request from charities: contact, EIN, legal name, mailing address, mission; no bank fields

key_quote: If you doubt the authenticity of any correspondence claiming to originate from Vanguard Charitable, please call us at 888-383-4483.
reading: Lists schemes against nonprofits: in-person grant offers, overpayment-and-refund, admin fees, lotteries, forwarding money, gift-card grants [F]. No item on payment-redirection or bank-change requests [F]
notes: Says 'we have seen a rise in fraudulent attempts against nonprofits'

key_quote: Vanguard Charitable sends confirmation letters or emails when changes occur with your philanthropic account.
reading: Also: 'Vanguard Charitable never asks donors to share login credentials by email, phone, or text' [F]. Donor-side; not a grantee bank-change control [I]

key_quote: NPT partners with PayPal to this payment solution, which allows us to send grants electronically and near-instantaneously to nonprofits using PayPal’s platform.
reading: Same design as Vanguard: charity bank details at PayPal [I]. NPT guide (2024): grants up to $250,000 by PayPal or check; unaccepted PayPal grant expires after 14 days and is reissued by check [X]. No NPT page on bank-change verification or BEC found
notes: Guide: https://www.nptrust.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/A-Guide-to-your-Donor-Advised-Fund-NPT.pdf (repo, not re-read)

key_quote: checks and PayPal Grant Payments do not require grant makers to collect and retain this information.
reading: PayPal-authored study (survey of 300 PayPal Confirmed Charities): charities 'share bank information just once' with PayPal [F]. Concentrates the bank-change attack surface at PayPal's account security [I]
notes: Vendor-authored; not an independent control description

reading: Search snippets: enrolment needs a PayPal business account, a confirmed charity account and agreement to PPGF terms; charity status confirmed by linking a charity bank account, else documents [R]. No bank-change or BEC procedure seen
notes: paypal.com robots.txt allows these paths; the server returned 403 to fetches (as in batch 36A)

provider_role: EFT rail (receiving account) and disbursement processor
key_quote: Once verified, your Chariot account uses non-debitable account and routing numbers — these cannot be used to pull money from your account
reading: Grants land in an account in the nonprofit's name; payers never hold the charity's operating-bank details [F/I]. Page explains why DAF fraud is common: gifts 'arrive without notice' and interception 'can go unnoticed' [F]
notes: One-time CIP/CDD verification; data held by Footprint

rail: Chariot Deposit Account -> External Financial Account
key_quote: Only Account Owners can add or update external financial account details.
reading: Where the account name cannot be matched to the organisation, Chariot 'may' ask for a bank statement or photo ID [F]. No callback or cooling-off period stated [F]
notes: Admins can transfer funds but not change the EFA (Account FAQs)

key_quote: Two-factor authentication (TFA) is required for all Chariot accounts to protect your organization’s data and funds.
reading: Owner TFA reset needs identity verification and Chariot approval; ownership transfer needs the new owner to accept by email and 'complete identity verification' ([ownership transfers](https://help.givechariot.com/account-management/ownership-transfers.md)) [F]
notes: Money-movement notifications exist but are per-user opt-in/out (notifications page)

key_quote: Instead of simply validating payment pointers (account/routing numbers) using bank statements, Chariot focuses on validating officer identities through IRS master files and top-tier identity verification providers.
reading: Check path: validation 'based on donation amount, prior payment history, and address verification', 'direct contact for larger payments', Positive Pay and delivery tracking [F]. Stop-payment API for checks [F]
notes: Only processor that publishes a check-path risk engine and a larger-payment direct-contact step

key_quote: Organizations that have not claimed a Chariot profile will continue to receive Daffy donations by US Mail.
reading: Electronic grants go only to the charity's Chariot Deposit Account [F]. Daffy itself holds no charity bank details on these pages [I]

key_quote: To request changes to a charity's Daffy profile, create a Charity Updates ticket
reading: Required: Daffy link or EIN and US mailing address; no bank field [F]. A donor or anyone can request a mailing-address change; the verification applied is not stated [F/I]
notes: Mailed-check redirection vector if address changes are not verified [I]

key_quote: If a mailed donation has not been received, Daffy can cancel the original check and reissue a new one.

reading: dafgiving360.org and schwabcharitable.org return 403 to robots.txt, so not fetched. No grantee bank-change or BEC text found in search results
notes: 2024 policies say grants are paid 'by issuing checks' (batch 36C [X])

key_quote: Independently verify every request to change banking or payment information by calling/videoconferencing a known contact using a previously established method of communication—not a number contained in the request.
reading: Also: 'Require dual approval and separation of duties for grantee/contractor payment setup, banking changes' [F]. Used here as the scoring yardstick for PR01-PR23
notes: oig.doc.gov robots.txt returned 404 (no rules)
